question.text: What was the Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirement at issue in the Polson Ltd case?

answer.text: 25% public shareholding as mandated under Rule 19A of SCRR as a continuous listing requirement
51% public shareholding for all listed companies

explanation.text: The Logic: In the Polson Ltd case, BSE confirmed compliance with the 25% minimum public shareholding requirement mandated under Rule 19A of SCRR as a continuous listing requirement. The company achieved compliance using the Offer for Sale (OFS) mechanism, after a period of delayed compliance, and the matter was eventually settled. The Trap: MPS is 25%, not a higher figure such as 51% or 75%, and it operates as a continuous listing requirement rather than only an IPO-stage requirement. Note: The workbook describes the Polson facts in terms of 25% MPS under Rule 19A, OFS-based compliance, delayed compliance and settlement. Broader corrective-action menus (rights issue or other SEBI-approved mechanisms) go beyond the page-level evidence.
